artists.biography:
Tangerine Dream is a German electronic music group founded in 1967 by Edgar Froese. The band has undergone many personnel changes over the years, with Froese being the only continuous member. Drummer and composer Klaus Schulze was briefly a member of an early lineup, but the most stable version of the group, during their influential mid-1970s period, was as a keyboard trio with Froese, Christopher Franke, and Peter Baumann. Early in the 1980s, Johannes Schmoelling replaced Baumann, and this lineup, too, was stable and extremely productive.
Tangerine Dream's early "Pink Years" albums had a pivotal role in the development of Krautrock. Their "Virgin Years" and later albums became a defining influence in the genre known as New Age music, although the band themselves disliked the term.
Although the group has released numerous studio and live recordings, a substantial number of their fans were introduced to Tangerine Dream by their film soundtracks, which total over sixty and include Sorcerer, Thief, The Keep, Risky Business, Firestarter, Legend, Near Dark, Shy People, and Miracle Mile.

perplexity.description:
Released on February 25, 2022, Raum is the 125th official album by pioneering electronic group Tangerine Dream and their second studio album following the passing of founder Edgar Froese in 2015. The album was composed and produced by the current lineup—Thorsten Quaeschning, Hoshiko Yamane, and Paul Frick—with full access to Froese’s archives, blending late-night real-time compositions and classic studio techniques. Musically, Raum features sequencer-driven soundscapes, warm synthesizers, and ambient textures, with nods to the band’s early live studio works such as Zeit and Phaedra. Standout tracks include the 17-minute “In 256 Zeichen,” the acid-tinged “Continuum,” and the title track “Raum,” which highlights a Moog Minitaur sequence and Yamane’s violin, creating a bridge between the band’s past and present.

Raum continues Tangerine Dream’s legacy of evolving electronic music, maintaining deep respect for their five-decade history while exploring new sonic territories. The album’s structure and abstract, amorphous nature have been noted by critics for creating a warm, pulsating atmosphere, even if some tracks are seen as less memorable individually. Released through Kscope, Raum received positive reviews for its harmonious and immersive qualities, with outlets like Resident Advisor praising it as one of the band’s best records in decades. The album stands as a significant entry in their discography, reflecting both the group’s enduring influence and their ability to innovate within the electronic genre.
